transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-02 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Markus Patel (Redwood SE), Jenna Park (AtlasHealth SRE), Luis Ortega (Platform Eng), Priya Malhotra (Security)

Summary: short weekly check-in to close out access blockers for staging pilot.

[00:00] Ava: hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have a shorter agenda today, main goal is to make sure staging access is green and we can run the smoke tests next week
[00:22] Jenna: yep thanks Ava, i only have about 45 minutes so i'll try to keep it tight — first question, are you still expecting us to provide the exact CIDR range for the gateway, or can you accept tags from our cloud account?
[00:38] Markus: we can accept both, but for the smoke tests we prefer explicit CIDR so our routing and egress rules are deterministic. tags are okay for long term, but for this POC if you can provide the CIDR it speeds up firewall rule verification
[00:52] Luis: okay that we can do, there might be a corporate proxy in the path though; i'll confirm exact egress ip ranges — might be as few as two ips but could be a small block
[01:10] Ava: perfect, Jenna if you can put that in the infra ticket that'd be great. also, quick note on naming: our console reference is "Redwood Dedicated" but sometimes our docs say "Redwood Dedi" — sorry if that causes confusion in the packet names
[01:30] Priya: quick security note, we need to know if you are going to integrate with our KMS for the pilot or if you'll manage keys in your side — we prefer KMS but need to confirm policy constraints
[01:46] Markus: KMS on customer side is fine, we've done both. We will need a service account with decrypt permissions and a short-lived role for the gateway. we'll provide an example IAM policy in the KMS doc
[02:02] Jenna: when you say "short-lived role" do you mean rotating creds, or something like a STS token?
[02:10] Markus: typically STS tokens, yeah. we tend to exchange a signed token to the gateway and rotate every hour in pilot mode. but we can match whatever you require for compliance
[02:25] Ava: Priya, i'll send the KMS integration doc and SOC2 redacted pack after this call, i think that should help answer the HSM / rotation questions
[02:36] Priya: yep please do. our main check is can we see the key usage audit / can we revoke quickly — and also whether keys are ever exportable from the HSM
[02:48] Markus: keys are never exportable if you're using a customer-managed KMS with HSM. if you go with our managed key path it's similar but we will provide attestations — i'll put notes in the doc and clarify the difference
[03:05] Ava: great. moving on, we wanted to clarify the SSO flow — Jenna, you mentioned you have a SAML IdP. do you have an admin contact who can accept the test SP metadata?
[03:20] Jenna: yes, we have an SSO admin (Sarah) but she's out this week. i can provide Sarah's backup (Raj) who can take the metadata and return the cert. i will add contact info to the ticket
[03:34] Luis: we also need to ensure roles map correctly — e.g., who gets access to the redwood console vs just the gateway logs — can you outline the RBAC mapping?
[03:46] Markus: absolutely. our default RBAC is coarse for pilots: admin vs viewer. we can create custom roles but that usually comes after sign-off. for now we'll map a few test users to admin and viewer so you can validate access flows
[04:02] Jenna: that works for now. next, about the gateway creds, is the plan to expose a single ingress endpoint from our staging VPC to your gateway or do you want us to proxy through a customer-managed ENI?
[04:18] Ava: for the POC the simplest is single ingress with allowlist on CIDR. If you need an ENI and private link we can discuss as a next step but that takes longer
[04:28] Luis: noted — single ingress is easier. i will check with network ops about any NAT/masquerade quirks
[04:40] Markus: also wanted to flag that our runtime has a prefix cache (we sometimes call it KV-cache, pronounced kay-vee cache) that helps reduce token cost for repeat prompts. for the benchmark we planned three prompt shapes — short, mid, long — to show latency and cost delta
[04:58] Jenna: sorry i missed earlier where the cache lives — is that in your gateway or in the model instance?
[05:05] Markus: partly in the gateway and partly in the serving runtime. technically we store recency in the KV layer near the model to avoid extra round trips, but from your perspective it's opaque — you'll see lower tail latency on repeated prefixes
[05:18] Priya: is any user content persisted outside your logs? data residency is a big ask for us
[05:25] Ava: we store request logs for debugging for a limited retention that we agreed in the pilot; we'll redact PII and can sign a data handling addendum. i'll include the retention window in the security pack
[05:38] Priya: okay, make sure the addendum mentions the redaction approach — sometimes automated redaction misses patient ids
[05:47] Markus: understood. we'll include an explicit step to support a manual review process for flagged items during the POC
[05:55] Ava: moving to benchmarks — Markus, you were going to do a quick run on staging after we get CIDR and SSO? timeline?
[06:05] Markus: i can do a 15-minute baseline this week if we have the egress ip and the gateway accessible. i'll capture p50/p95 and token-count cost estimate and drop the trace into the shared sheet
[06:16] Jenna: as long as it's not destructive go ahead; we'll schedule the window — prefer Wednesday morning 9-10am PT
[06:24] Ava: sounds good, we'll tentatively book that. next, any blockers from your side for the smoke test?
[06:31] Luis: firewall rules are the main one. also we have an internal proxy that rewrites headers sometimes; if your gateway expects original headers we need to coordinate with infra to pass-through or add x-forwarded-for rules
[06:45] Markus: we can accept x-forwarded-for, but sometimes signature verification ties to the original ip. we'll document the header expectations and a fallback plan in the integration guide
[06:58] Jenna: okay, i'll wait for that doc. next question: do you require a dedicated model pin for the POC or can we use your hosted variant?
[07:10] Ava: for performance predictability we recommend a pinned model on dedicated capacity but for speed you can use hosted. given AtlasHealth's compliance needs i'd recommend dedicated or private deployment, but for the initial smoke test hosted with pinned version is fine
[07:28] Priya: dedicated is preferable if we can get the right contractual terms — can you share SLA for latency and uptime for dedicated?
[07:36] Ava: yes, dedicated SLAs are in the pricing packet but i'll surface the latency SLOs specifically in the summary doc. note dedicated tends to have lower inter-request jitter since it's not multi-tenant
[07:50] Luis: one more infra nit — do you support private subnet peering or do you expect a public egress?
[07:58] Markus: both patterns are supported. private peering needs an additional setup window with networking but avoids public egress; public egress is faster to spin up. for the POC, public egress with allowlist is the fastest path
[08:12] Jenna: fine, we'll do public egress for now. i also have a quick question about logging retention — how long do you keep request bodies by default?
[08:21] Ava: default is 30 days for pilot, we can shorten to 7 days on request; logs are encrypted at rest and access-controlled
[08:31] Priya: can you log to our SIEM? it's often a compliance ask to have logs forwarded
[08:35] Markus: yes we can stream logs to your SIEM using secure push, we have connectors for common systems. i'll list supported SIEM targets in the integration guide
[08:47] Ava: okay actionable items recap — Jenna to provide CIDR and SSO backup contact; Priya will confirm KMS constraints; Luis will check firewall/proxy; Markus to run KV-cache baseline once we have access; Ava will send security docs
[09:02] Jenna: quick note, when you say KV-cache baseline what metrics exactly will you share?
[09:08] Markus: i'll capture p50, p95 latency, tokens per response, and a micro-cost delta estimate plus a small trace for one transaction per prompt shape so you can see the timing breakdown
[09:22] Luis: please include TCPTLS handshake time if possible — our proxy can add a non-trivial overhead
[09:29] Markus: will do, we'll annotate the trace
[09:33] Ava: any competitors or alternate vendors you are looking at so we can tailor the doc?
[09:37] Priya: we've had a call with Anthropic last month and also looking at a hosted route with OpenAI for less sensitive workloads. nothing decided yet
[09:48] Ava: understood; we'll make sure the security pack addresses the questions you have about key management and audit logs versus what they offered
[09:57] Jenna: timeline check — after smoke-test and doc review we expect an internal review with legal the following week; so getting docs this Friday would be ideal
[10:07] Ava: noted, sending Friday. ok any other blockers?
[10:12] Luis: i will run a quick connectivity pre-check with routing team and update the ticket tonight
[10:17] Priya: one more thought — encryption in transit: do you support mutual TLS for the gateway?
[10:23] Markus: yes we support mTLS and client certs; for pilots it's optional but we can enable it if you want. note that mTLS will require extra steps for cert management on your side
[10:36] Jenna: might be easier to start without mTLS and enable it for the dedicated phase
[10:42] Ava: agreed. last part, can we confirm the smoke-test goal: 1) establish TLS connection and SSO login, 2) perform three prompt shapes and capture p50/p95, 3) validate log delivery to SIEM. is that correct?
[10:57] Markus: yep that's exactly the checklist
[11:02] Jenna: sounds good. feel comfortable with that plan. i'll coordinate the 9am Wednesday window
[11:08] Ava: perfect. closing notes — i'll send the docs and update the calendar with the smoke-test slot. thanks everyone
[11:15] (call wraps with some quick side comments about next week's demo and a reminder to review the shared sheet)

Transcription notes: occasional mis-heard names and acronyms, e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "kay vee cash", "Redwood Dedicated" near docs spelled "Redwood Dedi" in one slide.

End of recording.
file_notes: Meeting captured via Fireflies. Attendees agreed to a Wednesday morning smoke test pending CIDR/SSO handoff. Security questions prioritized: KMS rotation, log retention, SIEM forwarding.
